Partly because of dial up speeds, but a large part because of the lack of available digital images.

I justified it as a working expense. I was making good money on the side creating web pages. Being able to take a picture of their business, and have it on a sample page to demonstrate sold a number of folks on it.

Here's the problem. I got so much crap from other photographers with "real" cameras, who dismissed the very notion of digital images, that I became more entrenched. I used that camera for everything.

I don't know why, but the phrase "no shit" came to mind when I read that. It's almost as though it's not a science at all, since you can never have a control.

Whatever though, these guys are really smart and I'm sure they figured out how to do lots of science without all that extra bullshit non-economists seem to require for scientific endeavors. The sooner they can tell us how to organize one of the most important systems in our global society, the better, and I certainly don't need to know anything about how they come to their conclusions.

Even if "they" give us the best answer on how to run society, we still have to implement it.

Its that second part that really worries me.

Yeah, well it should, given that implementing things that are likely impossible is probably going to be pretty difficult. You can only actually implement a system that's going to work correctly, otherwise you get...well, what we have now for the most part.

Human minds can't model economies, only elements of them, thus we have no working models of an economy.

I disagree. We can model economics. We just havent quite figured it out yet. I think we need a more dynamic system that flows between main sectors of economic throught because the economy is acting differently at different times, and for different reasons. Being Keynesinan, behavioral, Austrian School, or anything else is bad if all you do is study your own idea and implement policy based on one factor. There are a myriad of ideas out there with good models, we just need to decide which ones to use when, and in the most appropriate circumstance.

We can model economics. We just havent quite figured it out yet.

If by "we", you mean "a potential future artificial-intelligence with the scope and ability to cohesively bring together seeming random and unrelated data sets into a relevant and actionable body of information capable of systemically addressing any situation involving value and the exchange of objects or services related to value" then I'm totally with you. If you meant people and their brains though, I'm less optimistic, and in fact I'm not even convinced we've really begun to identify what kind of a "problem" is being studied.
